correctness.rationale: The Heyting implication is reconstructed as a principal-downset condition; Peirce holds iff the union of strict predecessors of minimal excluded points is contained in B. Counting consequent ideals proves the general sum. Each nonempty proper antecedent in a least-point poset fails with B=empty, and a chain of three creates a second failure. The greatest-point argument fixes the unique coatom and compares all other antecedents. Both equality directions and the two-level formula are proved explicitly. Finite tests compare direct implication and boundary calculations for 5,231 naturally labeled posets.

value.rationale: Bumpus–Kocsis qualitative Peirce no-gap theorem motivates extracting rates. The exact universal order-theoretic formula and rigid sharp h-2 class bound for finite rooted/co-rooted frames answer natural numerical questions and identify precisely which stars have the smallest possible defect, with a two-sided branching penalty on complete height-two frames. This is not mere rewriting of the known qualitative no-gap statement; no universal all-Heyting h-2 claim is made.
